# Pagination Checklist: Complete Ingredient Listings

**Purpose**: Review the completeness, clarity, consistency, and testability of ingredient-listing requirements.
**Created**: 2026-10-06
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

## Requirement Completeness

- [ ] CHK001 Are the ingredient catalog, inventory, plan, preparation, and recipe views all explicitly in scope? [Completeness, Spec §FR-001–003]
- [ ] CHK002 Are the expected outcomes when later-page retrieval fails specified for each page's existing failure behavior? [Coverage, Spec §FR-005–006]

## Requirement Clarity

- [ ] CHK003 Are the 100-item page size, 50-page limit, and overflow behavior defined at the appropriate design level? [Clarity, Plan §Constraints]
- [ ] CHK004 Are preservation of non-pagination query parameters and replacement of the page-size parameter stated clearly? [Clarity, Plan §Architecture]

## Requirement Consistency

- [ ] CHK005 Are completeness, ordering, household visibility, and filtering described consistently across all five views? [Consistency, Spec §FR-001–004]
- [ ] CHK006 Are complete-list guarantees consistent with the stated absence of a snapshot when the catalog changes during retrieval? [Consistency, Spec §Edge Cases; §Assumptions]

## Acceptance Criteria Quality

- [ ] CHK007 Can completeness be objectively measured by checking all 140 entries for omissions and duplicates? [Measurability, Spec §SC-001; §SC-003]
- [ ] CHK008 Is the helper's failure/no-partial-return behavior distinguishable from successful completion while each page retains its existing fallback? [Measurability, Spec §SC-005]

## Scenario Coverage

- [ ] CHK009 Do independent scenarios cover catalog and inventory listings as well as ingredient-name resolution in plan, preparation, and recipe views? [Coverage, Spec §US1–US2]
- [ ] CHK010 Are existing search, dimension, global-visibility, and household-visibility filters accounted for during continuation? [Coverage, Spec §FR-004]

## Edge Case Coverage

- [ ] CHK011 Are empty catalogs, exact batch boundaries, a failure after an earlier successful page, and continuation overflow addressed? [Coverage, Spec §Edge Cases; Plan §Constraints]
- [ ] CHK012 Is the expected behavior for catalog changes during retrieval explicitly bounded? [Clarity, Spec §Edge Cases]

## Non-Functional Requirements

- [ ] CHK013 Are household access controls and protection of private ingredient information stated without conflicting with server-side retrieval? [Security, Spec §FR-007; Plan §Constraints]
- [ ] CHK014 Is the scale target sufficient to judge the 100-item page size and 50-page safety bound? [Performance, Spec §SC-001; Plan §Technical Context]

## Dependencies and Assumptions

- [ ] CHK015 Is the dependency on the API cursor contract and the required API-before-Web rollout order explicit? [Dependency, Spec §Assumptions; Plan §API Contract Sequence]

## Ambiguities and Conflicts

- [ ] CHK016 Is “every ingredient visible to the active household” precise about household-owned and globally visible ingredients? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-001; §FR-004]

## Notes

- Items assess the quality of the written requirements and plan, not whether implementation or tests pass.
- Leave items unchecked until the reviewer approves each requirements-quality criterion.
- `/speckit-implement` reads checklist state as a gate and must not modify markers.
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `/speckit-specify` and `/speckit-clarify`.
